title: Dad and the highlighter
summary: Your first proper contract is on the kitchen table and your dad has taken a day off work to read it with a highlighter. A season on, he still has his copy.

ends.title: His copy
ends.text: Your dad read your first contract line by line, and he still has the copy he highlighted.

ends.title: Signed it alone
ends.text: You signed your first contract without him. He found out from the club's website.

beats.title: The kitchen table

event.title: The kitchen table
event.speaker: dad
setup: Your first professional contract is on the kitchen table, eleven pages. Your dad has a yellow highlighter, his reading glasses and a day off work he booked a month ago.

say: "I just want to go through it. I'm not saying there's anything wrong. Page four, what does image rights mean? Is that your face?"

replies.label: Sign it while he's on page four.

say: He takes his glasses off. "I know he has. I'd like to and all. I've never read one before."

read.text: It takes three hours. He highlights eleven things and rings the club about one of them himself. They change a word. He's unbearable about it for a month.

signed.text: You sign it on the side. He puts the highlighter back in the drawer with the batteries and says well done.

beats.hint: Your first contract is on the table

event.title: The glovebox
event.speaker: dad
setup: A season on. You borrow your dad's van to move a sofa. In the glovebox, under the tax disc and the mints, is a folded contract with yellow lines all over it.
{if arc.path=='signed'}It's your contract. He must have printed his own copy off.{/if}

outcomes.text: "Somebody had to read it properly," he says. He shows you page four. He's written "FACE" in the margin.

choices.label: Put it back where it was.

outcomes.text: You put it back under the mints. He never knows you saw it.
You put it back under the mints and drive the sofa round to your flat.
